topic: What frequency planning challenges arise when coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows?
consensus_response: When coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows, co-frequency, codirectional NGSO satellites cause reduced spectral efficiency and capacity reductions due to in-line events interference. This leads to increased system complexity for advanced signal processing and coordination protocols, resulting in higher power allocation costs and reduced capacity. Dynamic frequency planning becomes essential to adapt to changing satellite positions and interference patterns in real-time.
reference_context: The reference context highlights specific challenges for parallel satellite and terrestrial link scenarios, including the need for coordination to mitigate in-line events interference between NGSO satellites and GSO satellites or other NGSO satellites. The increasing number of satellites deployed in each constellation demands efficient use of the available spectrum, driving research on more efficient frequency allocation techniques.
